messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: fma() and errors
parts:
Also, I think we want the basic arithmetic
functions like fma() to just propagate the
basic arithmetic operator behaviors, not
check for NaN, so that

fma(x,y,z);

behaves exactly the same way as

x * y + z;

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] fma() and errors
parts:
I thought about this a bit more and realized
that we'd been talking about being able to
just turn all the error checking on and off.
In that situation, we might want to add error
checking to everything.

Also, I think we can cut down on the implementations
with templates. The top-level fma() function with
policy defaults can be handled just as for the normal
log density function. This also saves having to generate
new items on the stack, which we definitely don't want
to do with these kinds of low-level functions.

Daniel and I can sort this out in a way that should
be transparent from the outside.

Also, we haven't decided how to remove bounds, overflow, and
domain checking. Should we add our own property or use
NDEBUG? I don't know much about how C++ projects get built
at this level of detail.

- Bob
